title: Sunset playbook for legacy streaming-socket API and companion model alias mapping
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Define and execute a low-risk, observable retirement of the legacy real-time streaming socket API (legacy socket handshake + /v0/chat-socket model aliases) and provide clear companion mapping rules to the unified HTTP streaming endpoints and model aliases. This ticket covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, migration playbook for SDKs, and staged timeline for customers and partners.
background: We maintain an older socket-based streaming protocol that a subset of customers still use. In parallel we've standardized on the unified HTTP streaming API and a simpler model aliasing scheme. Keeping the legacy socket increases maintenance burden and delays runtime optimizations (batching, KV cache warmup) for streaming workloads. Prior inspections show ~6% of active customers use the socket protocol; most are small-volume integrations or legacy client versions.
scope_changes: This PRD initially proposed immediate cutover; after stakeholder review the scope was reduced to a phased deprecation with a 9-month timeline and SDK-assisted migrations. It now includes: automated alias translation rules, SDK runtime patches to emulate legacy chunk format, and a short-term compatibility shim for customers unable to update immediately.
migration_plan: Inventory: query usage telemetry to produce a list of active socket clients by org and SDK version.
Alias mapping: publish a canonical mapping table from legacy model aliases (chatstream-*, realtime-*) to unified model ids and recommended quantization profiles.
SDK patches: ship minor SDK releases that intercept legacy socket handshake and transparently upgrade to the HTTP streaming endpoint with minimal client code change.
Compatibility shim: deploy a 6-month server-side compatibility shim that accepts legacy handshake and proxies to unified runtime; log deprecated usage and add throttled warnings.
Documentation: publish a migration guide with code snippets (Node/Python/Go), sample responses, and troubleshooting steps.
Communication: notify affected customers in three waves (30/90/180 days) with migration playbooks and offer migration assistance for high-value customers.
Telemetry & gating: add telemetry events for successful migrations, failure modes, and latency regressions; define rollback triggers for regressions.
Shutdown: schedule a hard shutdown date after the shim retirement; provide clear fallback guidance (downgrade to supported HTTP streams or dedicated capacity options).
rollout_timeline: Day 0: Publish RFC and mapping table internally; start customer inventory queries (done).
Week 2: Release SDK minor versions with in-process upgrade behavior and opt-in telemetry; begin internal canary with Platform team.
Month 1: Public docs & migration guide; first customer email wave to high-impact orgs with recommended actions.
Month 3: Enable server-side compatibility shim in all regions; watch telemetry; second customer reminder with migration checklist.
Month 6: Begin deprecation enforcement mode—start soft throttling for legacy handshake for new connections; third customer reminder and support push.
Month 9: Turn off shim entirely and redirect legacy hostnames to a deprecation landing page; start automatic badge for migrated status in Console.
Month 12: Hard removal from runtime and archive alias mappings; final post-mortem and lessons learned.
Dates are target estimates and will be adjusted based on telemetry during canary phases.
monitoring_and_success_metrics: Reduction in active legacy socket clients to <1% of baseline prior to shim shutdown.
95th percentile tail latency parity between migrated traffic and baseline unified streams within 15%.
Zero critical production regressions attributable to migration in the two weeks after each major rollout step.
Migration completion rate: >80% of targeted high-impact customers migrated by Month 6.
SDK adoption metric: percentage of traffic using patched SDK versions reaches 75% within 3 months of release.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Some customers run air-gapped or heavily regulated deployments and cannot update clients quickly. Mitigation: offer private deployment patches and coordinate with Sales/CS for extended timelines.

Risk: Compatibility shim may leak implementation-specific behavior causing hidden regressions. Mitigation: limit shim feature surface, add end-to-end tests mirroring popular client flows, and maintain a short retention policy for shim logs.

Risk: Automated mapping from legacy aliases to new model IDs may produce subtle quality regressions. Mitigation: include recommended quantization and sampling profiles; run a small AB test on quality metrics before mass mapping.
Risk: Customer confusion due to duplicate deprecation notices. Mitigation: centralize communication via Console banners, a single deprecation FAQ, and account-level migration dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Published and reviewed public migration guide with code samples in Node, Python, and Go.
A2: SDK releases exist that can transparently upgrade legacy socket handshake to unified HTTP streaming without code changes for 95% of current client patterns.
A3: Compatibility shim deployed behind a feature flag in production with telemetry gating and has completed a 2-week canary with no regressions.
A4: Customer inventory identifies all active orgs and a migration plan is scheduled for any org with >1% of their traffic on the legacy socket.
A5: Rollout timeline and communication plan approved by Security, Support, Sales, and Platform teams.
A6: Monitoring dashboards for migration progress, latency, and error-rate regressions are live and documented.
A7: Legal and Compliance sign-off obtained for customers on Private deployments where we will provide bespoke migration assistance.
customer_communication: Wave 1 (30 days): Personalized emails to top 50 affected orgs with migration playbook and offer for 1:1 migration help.
Wave 2 (90 days): Broadcast in-product banner and knowledge base article; invite to migration office hours.
Wave 3 (180 days): Final reminder and scheduled automatic SDK patch rollout (opt-out available for enterprise customers).
dependencies: ENG-9175: telemetry events and migration dashboard
ENG-9250: SDK patch releases (node, python, go)
SEC-301: Compliance review for private deployment assistance
